title: Tabular data: clean, join, group, and validate
sources: pandas documentation concepts: DataFrame, indexing, merge, groupby, missing data
masterChecklist: pandas-style tabular data concepts: indexing, joins, group operations, missing data, time series, data-quality checks
whyItMatters: Most business data arrives as tables. Reliable analysis depends on understanding rows, columns, missing values, join keys, and grouped calculations before making a chart or decision.
simpleExplanation: A table has rows and named columns. A join combines tables using matching keys. Grouping calculates summaries per category. Missing values are data states to investigate, not values to silently replace. Data-quality checks make assumptions visible.
mentalModel: Tables are spreadsheets with rules: a join matches filing cards by an ID, grouping makes one summary pile per category, and quality checks inspect whether the cards are complete and consistent.
outcomes: Explain a join key and duplicate-key risk.
Write simple quality questions before analysis.

realWorldExample.scenario: A learning analytics report joins lesson completions to learner records and counts completions by track.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: A duplicate join key can multiply rows. Filling missing values without understanding them can create false conclusions.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Check key uniqueness, row counts before and after joins, missing-value rates, and expected value ranges.

procedure: State the grain of each row: what does one row represent?

commonMistakes.mistake: Joining on a non-unique key without checking.
commonMistakes.avoid: Validate key expectations and inspect counts before and after merging.

commonMistakes.mistake: Replacing all missing values with zero.
commonMistakes.why: Missing can mean unknown, not applicable, delayed, or invalid.
commonMistakes.avoid: Choose a documented treatment based on the data meaning.

commonMistakes.why: Bad records become hidden inside aggregates.
